Contact

Contact Beat the Scam for editorial corrections, privacy questions, or partnership enquiries. We aim to respond to all editorial requests promptly.

For editorial contact or corrections, email editorial@beatthescam.com. For partnership enquiries, email hello@beatthescam.com. For privacy, legal, or security matters, please use the dedicated addresses below.

Editorial & correctionseditorial@beatthescam.com — send the page URL and the correction you want reviewed.
Advertising or partnershipshello@beatthescam.com — include the business name, proposal, and relevant website.
Privacy & data protectionprivacy@beatthescam.com — reference “Privacy request” in the subject line.
Legal & copyrightlegal@beatthescam.com — Terms, intellectual property, and reproduction requests.
Security disclosuresecurity@beatthescam.com — see also our security.txt.

To report a scam to UK authorities directly, use Report Fraud for England, Wales and Northern Ireland, or Police Scotland on 101 for Scotland. Ofcom says suspicious SMS texts can be forwarded to 7726 free of charge; use the relevant app's own reporting tool for non-SMS messages.
